messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: generating models for tests?
parts:
This one's mainly for Daniel, though it affects Michael and
the entire 2.0 refactor.

The way the tests are set up now is very brittle to changes
in the way the model code is generated.

There are a bunch of models that were generated by stanc
at some point just included in our test set, either as standalone
files or cut-and-pasted into other tests.

This means whenever I change the way the code is generated, I have
to change every one of these by hand, which is really slowing
me down. I haven't gotten through all of them yet, but what's
really bumming me out is that I'm going to have to do it all again.

Is there a way to instead save the models and have the tests
run stanc to generate?

- Bob

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] generating models for tests?
parts:
Yeah, if you let me know where they are, I can start generating them instead of having hard-coded models checked in.

I think there were two reasons for having hard-coded models:
1) I couldn't figure out how to generate on the fly at the time.
2) It tests the behavior of our internal classes independent of the generator.

If we've got enough coverage now, I think we can drop the second concern.


Daniel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] generating models for tests?
parts:
On 7/15/13 10:34 AM, Daniel Lee wrote:
> Yeah, if you let me know where they are, I can start generating them instead of having hard-coded models checked in.
>
> I think there were two reasons for having hard-coded models:
> 1) I couldn't figure out how to generate on the fly at the time.
> 2) It tests the behavior of our internal classes independent of the generator.
>
> If we've got enough coverage now, I think we can drop the second concern.

Everything's OK for now, so it's a low priority.

For 1, we need to generate without the main so they can link by the
tests. I found out the hard way when debugging that the makefile
builds any .stan file into a .cpp file with a main, which kept
overwriting the version I'd compiled to .cpp without a main :-)

For 2, I all classes should be tested independently. I'd rather not
use auto-generated code to do that because it can override some of
the basic behavior and thus hide the proper tests.

After my model refactor gets committed, the internal classes are much
simpler as much of the functionality has been pushed out to
static functions.

- Bob
